definition.def: When you approach something, you get closer to it.
examples: He didn't approach the front door at once. [VERB noun]
When I approached, they grew silent. [VERB]
We turned to see the approaching car slow down. [VERB-ing]

definition.def: An approach to a place is a road, path, or other route that leads to it.
examples: The path serves as an approach to the boat house. [+ to]

definition.def: If you approach someone about something, you speak to them about it for the first time, often making an offer or request.
examples: When Chappel approached me about the job, my first reaction was disbelief. [VERB noun preposition]
He approached me to create and design the restaurant. [VERB noun to-infinitive]
Anna approached several builders and was fortunate to come across Eddie. [VERB noun]

definition.def: When you approach a task, problem, or situation in a particular way, you deal with it or think about it in that way.
examples: The Bank has approached the issue in a practical way. [VERB noun preposition/adverb]
Employers are interested in how you approach problems. [VERB noun]

definition.def: Your approach to a task, problem, or situation is the way you deal with it or think about it.
examples: We will be exploring different approaches to gathering information. [+ to]
...the adversarial approach of the British legal system.

definition.def: As a future time or event approaches, it gradually gets nearer as time passes.
examples: As autumn approached, the plants and colours in the garden changed. [VERB]

definition.def: As you approach a future time or event, time passes so that you get gradually nearer to it.
examples: We approach the end of the year with the economy slowing and little sign of cheer. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If something approaches a particular level or state, it almost reaches that level or state.
examples: Oil prices have approached their highest level for almost ten years. [VERB noun]
